findings.title: Migration crashes when embed_category setting is absent
findings.body: The migration does `execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. On any site that never set the `embed_category` site setting (it defaulted to blank), the query returns zero rows, so `[0]` is nil and calling `['id']` on nil raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration. The same fragility exists on line 15 for `uncategorized_category_id`. This will block upgrades for sites that used embeddable_hosts but never picked an embed category. Guard with `.first`/`&.` and a fallback.

findings.title: Migrated hosts are inserted raw, without the normalization the new model applies
findings.body: The old `embeddable_hosts` setting explicitly accepted values like `http://eviltrout.com` (the old `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` stripped `http(s)://` before comparing, and the removed specs confirm that format worked). The migration copies each line verbatim into the new table via raw SQL, bypassing the model's `before_validation` that strips the scheme and path. After migration, `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `URI(referer).host` (e.g. `eviltrout.com`) against the stored value `http://eviltrout.com` with `lower(host) = ?`, which never matches — embedding silently stops working for those hosts. The migration should normalize each value (strip scheme/path) before inserting.

findings.title: update/destroy raise NoMethodError for nonexistent host instead of 404
findings.body: `update` and `destroy` look up the record with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then call `host.destroy` / `host.save` without a nil check. A request for a missing or stale id (e.g. a row deleted in another tab) returns a 500 NoMethodError instead of a 404. Use `find` or raise `Discourse::NotFound` when the record is nil.

findings.title: before_validation calls sub! on possibly-nil host
findings.body: The `before_validation` callback does `self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')` unconditionally. If a record is saved without a host (or the admin client sends a blank value — the DB column is null: false but validation happens first), `self.host` is nil and `sub!` raises NoMethodError, producing a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard with `if self.host` (and rely on a presence/format validation to report the error).

findings.title: Host comparison is not case-insensitive on the input side
findings.body: `record_for_host` runs `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` but never downcases the `host` extracted from the URI, while the `before_validation` that stores records never downcases either (the format validation is case-insensitive). A stored host entered as `Example.COM` matches, but an incoming referer `HTTP://EXAMPLE.COM/path` yields `uri.host == "EXAMPLE.COM"`, which won't equal `lower(stored)`. Downcase both the stored value and the lookup value to make matching reliably case-insensitive.

findings.title: No uniqueness validation or DB index on host
findings.body: Nothing prevents two EmbeddableHost rows for the same host (with different categories), and there is no index on `host`. Duplicates make `record_for_host`'s `.first` nondeterministic — a host could resolve to either category for imported topics — and every embed check (`host_allowed?` runs on every embedded comments request) does a full table scan. Add `validates_uniqueness_of :host` and a unique (or at least plain) index on `host` in the migration.

findings.title: Fabricator file contents are swapped between category and embeddable_host files
findings.body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now defines the `:embeddable_host` fabricator, while the newly added `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains all the `:category` fabricators. The contents were pasted into the wrong files. Fabrication happens to load every file in the directory so specs still pass, but the misnamed files will confuse future edits and any tooling that maps fabricator names to files — swap the contents back.

findings.title: category_id is mass-assigned from params without existence check
findings.body: `host.category_id = params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]` accepts any integer. An invalid id is only silently replaced with the uncategorized category when blank, not when pointing to a nonexistent category, leaving an orphaned foreign key; the admin UI will then break when rendering the host's category. Validate that the category exists (e.g. `validates :category, presence: true` with a foreign-key constraint) before saving.

findings.title: Embedded *_ids hydration can produce undefined entries
findings.body: In `_hydrateEmbedded`, for plural `*_ids` keys the code maps ids through `_lookupSubType`, which returns `undefined` when the id isn't present in the root payload, and then assigns the array to the plural property (the `hydrated || []` fallback never triggers since `map` always returns an array). Any payload whose `foo_ids` references an id not included in the sideloaded collection yields an array containing `undefined`, which will crash consumers doing `array[0].get('id')`. Filter out undefined values before assigning.
